maryland.framework: 2025 Revised Maryland College and Career Ready Standards for Mathematics

targets.scope: Apply properties of operations to add, subtract, factor, and expand linear expressions with rational coefficients.
Rewrite expressions in different forms to illuminate context and relationships.
Choose equation versus inequality for a context and justify the choice.
Write and solve contextual equations of Grade 7 forms using rational numbers; explain and interpret solutions.
Write and solve contextual inequalities of Grade 7 forms; graph and interpret solution sets.

mcps.unit: Math 7 Unit 6 — Expressions, Equations, and Inequalities
topics: Represent situations of the form px+q=r and p(x+q)=r

reuse_audit.scope_boundary: No new canonical ID, no registry activation, no changes to existing seed/mappings. Draft package deepens student usability and evidence only.

learning_goal: Model, solve, explain, graph, and interpret Maryland Grade 7 expressions, equations, and inequalities in context, using exact rational reasoning and equality/inequality-preserving transformations.

teaching_flow.learner_action: Inspect a context model (equal groups, fixed fee, target or constraint). Identify quantities, units, fixed amounts, per-unit rates, and whether the relationship describes an exact total or a range.
Predict equation vs inequality, estimate the solution or boundary, and explain which words in the context justify the model choice.

Apply the same inverse operation to both sides; for p(x+q)=r connect undoing multiplication first to the equal-groups model. For inequalities, preserve order under positive division and represent the resulting set on a number line.
Explain each step, substitute back into the original equation or inequality, and connect the numerical result to the context and units.
Complete seeded equation, inequality, model-choice, and equivalent-expression tasks with progressively faded scaffolds.
Use misconception-specific prompts for model-choice, grouping, distribution, inverse-operation, endpoint, graph-direction, and context-interpretation errors; repair with a fresh task.
From an unfamiliar Maryland-style situation, choose equation or inequality without a supplied template, construct the model, solve, graph if needed, and justify reasonable values.
Complete a disjoint unseen variant with hidden oracle. Guided work, hints, or teacher/LLM assistance cannot produce mastery evidence.

misconception_branches.evidence: Learner models 'exactly' with an inequality or 'at least/no more than' with an equation.
socratic: Does the context allow one exact total or a range of acceptable totals?
Which phrase—exactly, at least, no more than, more than—tells you the relationship type?
misconception_branches.repair: Contrast two near-identical contexts: 'exactly $80' versus 'at least $80'; write one equation and one inequality and explain the difference.

misconception_branches.evidence: Learner swaps fixed amount and per-unit coefficient, or places q outside p(x+q) incorrectly.
socratic: Which amount repeats for every group/unit?
If there are p identical groups, what entire quantity is repeated p times?
misconception_branches.repair: Build a tape/equal-groups model first, then translate it to px+q or p(x+q).

misconception_branches.evidence: Learner distributes p to only x or only q.
socratic: How many copies of x are there? How many copies of q?
Can you expand p(x+q) as repeated addition before using symbols?
misconception_branches.repair: Use 3(x+4)=3x+12 with tiles/repeated groups; then complete a fresh rational-coefficient example.

misconception_branches.evidence: Learner reverses the operation sequence or makes an arithmetic error isolating x.
socratic: What operation is outermost around x?
What inverse undoes that operation while preserving equality?
misconception_branches.repair: Annotate operation layers, undo them in reverse order, then verify by substitution into the original.

misconception_branches.evidence: Learner reports a solution without checking the original model.
socratic: What do both sides equal when your x is substituted?
Does that numerical check also make sense in the story?
misconception_branches.repair: Substitute into the original, not only the simplified line; state units/context.

misconception_branches.evidence: Learner uses open dot for ≤/≥ or closed dot for </>.
socratic: Does the boundary value itself satisfy the original statement?
Does 'at least' include equality? Does 'more than' include equality?
misconception_branches.repair: Test the boundary directly, then choose OPEN/CLOSED based on whether equality is allowed.

misconception_branches.evidence: Correct boundary but shades toward non-solutions.
socratic: Pick one value on each side of the boundary. Which one satisfies the original inequality?
misconception_branches.repair: Use a witness and counterexample before drawing the arrow.

misconception_branches.evidence: Learner gives a symbolic solution but does not restrict or interpret values in context.
socratic: Can the context use a negative or fractional count?
What does the boundary mean in words?
Which values are possible or reasonable?
misconception_branches.repair: Translate the symbolic set into an explicit contextual statement with units/domain.

independent_assessment.disjointness: Independent solution band is 12..24; guided band is 2..10, with mode embedded in RNG namespace and item ID.
requirements: No supplied symbolic setup in transfer contexts where modeling is the target.
Server-owned unseen state before any mastery decision.
Exact rational scoring and graph semantics verified server-side.
Written justification requires separately reviewed rubric; no LLM-only mastery judgment.
No assisted/guided attempt may back-credit independent mastery.

interactions: Equal-groups/tape model for p(x+q) versus px+q
Equation balance operations applied to both sides
Inequality number line with accessible OPEN/CLOSED endpoint and LEFT/RIGHT direction
Model-choice toggle equation/inequality with context phrase highlighting only in guided mode
Substitution table comparing original left/right expressions
Scaffold fading from concrete model to visual to symbolic
accessibility: keyboard equivalent for all drag/toggle controls
screen-reader announcement of each expression and transformation
